olivia: Quick check — I'm preparing a Terraform change that moves the staging secret for the LLM creds from SSM -> Secrets Manager and updates the k8s overlay to reference the new secret name. Two quick questions before I open the PR:

1) Do we need an explicit release gate change for the staging overlay (we currently gate on smoke tests + config drift)?
2) Any recommended migration steps to avoid pods trying to read the old SSM path during a rolling restart?

Current TF snippet I'm going to land:
```hcl
resource \"aws_secretsmanager_secret\" \"llm\" {
  name = \"redwood/llm/staging\"
}
resource \"aws_secretsmanager_secret_version\" \"llm_version\" {
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.llm.id
  secret_string = var.llm_creds_json
}
```
and kustomize patch I'm planning to add to overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml:
```yaml
- path: secret-patch.yaml
```
with secret-patch.yaml mounting `llm-credentials` in the deployment.

sam: quick thoughts — overall looks fine. couple of things: make sure you create the Secrets Manager secret (or a placeholder version) in the staging account before updating the k8s overlay. kubernetes will fail mounts if the secret doesn't exist during rollout. Also avoid changing the secret name in the same apply as updating the deployment; do it in two steps: create secret -> wait -> rollout update.

sam: small command set I run locally: 
```bash
# create placeholder secret (locally via aws cli assume role)
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name redwood/llm/staging --secret-string '{"dummy":"x"}' --region us-west-2
# then apply tf for the secret only
terraform apply -target=aws_secretsmanager_secret.llm -var-file=staging.tfvars
```

ton y: for gating — please add a preflight job that runs a simple `kubectl get secret llm-credentials -n staging` after the TF apply. Our release gate should require that preflight to succeed for the overlay promote to continue. For the canary rollout, use the existing overlay label `release/canary: true` and a Deployment strategy with `maxUnavailable: 0` + `maxSurge: 1` so we don't drop pods. Also consider a 10% canary traffic shift (we can reuse the ingress weight rule from `ingress-canary` job).

kevin: extra safety: add a small script to CI that scans manifests for `secretRef` entries and compares them against a list of allowed secret names for staging/prod. We had a couple of near-misses where a rename in TF broke mounts. tflint + a `scripts/verify-secret-refs.sh` that does `yq` checks should be enough. I can paste the script if you want.

deploy-bot: CI / preflight-checker: preflight job failed — `kubectl diff` reports missing secret `llm-credentials` in namespace `staging`. See: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/12345

olivia: thanks both — plan: I'll create the placeholder in staging via aws cli, run the TF apply for the secret only, then kick the preflight job and do a canary overlay apply. @sam — will ping you on the PR for a quick plan review. @kevin — would appreciate the verify-secret-refs script snip if you have it handy. :thumbsup:

sam: ack, I'll review once you push. keep the steps separate and add the preflight job in the PR so CI can catch it.

kevin: dropping a tiny `yq` snippet you can add to CI: 
```bash
# fail if manifest contains secretRef not in ALLOWED_SECRETS
ALLOWED=(llm-credentials other-allowed)
for s in $(git ls-files "overlays/staging/**/*.yaml"); do
  for ref in $(yq e '.. | select(has("secretRef")) | .secretRef // empty' $s); do
    if [[ ! " ${ALLOWED[*]} " =~ " ${ref} " ]]; then
      echo "Found unapproved secretRef: $ref in $s"; exit 1
    fi
  done
done
```

olivia: perfect — thanks everyone, I'll proceed and post the plan + CI run link in this thread.
